passage:
My name is Sunil, and I keep the accounts for a few small firms, Yogesh's included. This is what I saw last quarter.

Yogesh's company was two weeks late on salaries, then three. Dhruv, the lead developer, kept coming in anyway, and so did the rest of the team. At one meeting Dhruv said, "We believe in this." Yogesh looked pale.

Afterwards Yogesh sat with me over the ledger. "They are giving me loyalty I haven't earned yet. I'm not going to guilt them with it." He drew up a list: pay the salary dues first, before any supplier. Then he told the team the exact cash position.

Two weeks later, he wrote references for the two who took other jobs, and Dhruv stayed on with a plan for a small revised salary.

I don't know what Yogesh felt. But I know he never once said, "after all we've been through."

qa.q: Who is the lead developer that kept coming in?
qa.a: Dhruv is the lead developer who kept coming in.

qa.q: What did Yogesh feel about the team staying through late salaries?
qa.a: Yogesh felt the loyalty had not yet been earned and did not want to use it as a guilt lever, which is why Yogesh chose to be transparent.

qa.q: What did Yogesh do to honour the team's trust?
qa.a: Yogesh paid salary dues first, told the team the exact cash position and wrote references for those who left, without guilt-tripping anyone.

qa.q: How might Dhruv have seen the late salaries?
qa.a: Dhruv may have been worried but stayed out of belief in the company, so honest news and a fair plan helped Dhruv feel respected rather than used.

grounding: Yogesh receives staff loyalty through late salaries and honours it by being transparent, paying dues first and writing references, an accountant observing.

passage:
For three months, the salaries at Hrithik's small app studio in Hyderabad had come late. Simran, his first hire, never complained. She came in early, stayed late, and once brought him lunch when she saw he'd skipped it.
One evening, going through the accounts, Hrithik realised he had been counting on her staying. It felt like using her kindness. His stomach turned.
The next morning he called her in. "Simran, I owe you the truth. We might not survive past June. Your two months of pending salary gets paid first, before any vendor, by the end of this month. I've already written you a reference. If you want to look for another job, I will help, not hold it against you."
Simran stared at him. "I wasn't planning to leave."
"I know. That's exactly why I had to say it."
She smiled a little. "Then I'll stay till June. With my eyes open."

qa.q: How long had salaries been late at Hrithik's studio?
What was Hrithik feeling when he realised he was counting on Simran staying?
qa.a: He felt guilty and uneasy, his stomach turning, because it felt like using her kindness.

qa.q: How did Hrithik honour Simran's loyalty?
qa.a: He told her the truth about June, promised her pending salary first, wrote her a reference, and said he would help her find another job without guilt-tripping.

qa.q: How might Simran see Hrithik's honesty?
qa.a: Simran seems surprised but respected, and chooses to stay with her eyes open rather than out of blind loyalty.

grounding: An employee stays through late salaries; the founder is transparent, pays her dues first, writes a reference and refuses to guilt-trip her into staying.

passage:
"Nirmala, can you close the door for a minute?"
"Is it about the salary, Damini? It's fine, I know things are tight."
"It's not fine. It's the second month late. You've been here since we started, and you've never asked once."
"I believe in this place."
"I know you do. That's why I have to be honest. We have enough to pay what we owe you and the others by the fifteenth, and that's being paid first. After that, I don't know if we'll make it past August."
Nirmala looked at her hands. "Oh."
"I've written you a reference. It's in your inbox. If you get an offer, take it. I'd never want you to stay out of guilt."
"But what about you?"
"That's my risk to carry. Not yours."
Nirmala was quiet, then nodded. "Thank you for telling me straight."
"You earned that much. You earned more."

qa.q: By what date will Damini pay what she owes the staff?
What was Nirmala feeling when she said "Oh"?
qa.a: Nirmala felt shaken and worried, looking at her hands after hearing the company might not last past August.

qa.q: How did Damini treat Nirmala's loyalty with respect?
qa.a: Damini was transparent about the future, paid dues first, wrote a reference, and urged Nirmala to take any offer without guilt.

qa.q: How might Damini be feeling as she speaks?
qa.a: Damini seems guilty and responsible, which is why she insists the risk is hers to carry and not Nirmala's.

grounding: A founder is honest with a loyal employee about late salaries, pays dues first, writes a reference and never guilt-trips her into staying.
